1.explanation:
• Tabs/Tabs.mdx: shows the overall usage of the Tabs component and its overflow behavior, so you can see how and where overflow controls are rendered.
• Tab/Tab.mdx: describes the individual Tab API (label prop, id, and aria linking), which is analogous to how the overflow buttons should be labeled.
• TabContent/TabContent.mdx: illustrates how tab panels are linked to tabs via aria-controls and aria-labelledby, demonstrating the pattern for associating a visible label with a control.
• Button/Button.mdx: documents Button usage and best practices, including how to supply aria-labels to icon-only buttons to meet accessibility requirements.
• Button/button-avt.md: provides deeper guidance on the attributes and accessibility considerations for <button> elements, useful for understanding what ARIA props to add.
• FormLabel/FormLabel.mdx: covers how to correctly associate form controls with labels (via for= or aria-labelledby), which is the same pattern needed to give the overflow buttons an accessible name.
1.bug_scenario: When the Tabs component enters overflow mode (when the container width is reduced), left/right scroll buttons appear (class "bx--tab-overflow__btn") that allow the user to scroll through tab labels. Those buttons are rendered as <button> elements containing only an icon, with no visible text or <label> and with no aria-label or aria-labelledby attributes. As a result, accessibility tools report “Form control element <button> has no associated label” for each scroll arrow button, since there is no accessible name to convey their purpose.
